eva.name: Lunar 0.16 g partial gravity: LUCI, FM2, ZGF, SEA 8.2 psia, HALO (team campaign)
eva.hardware: NASA GRC free-fall centrifuge / LUCI sounding rocket / CLPS FM2 autonomous lunar payload / SoFIE (ISS MSG)
key_findings: 'Goldilocks' effect on the Moon (0.16 g): at 1 g strong buoyancy (~20-30 cm/s) cools and blows the flame off, while at 0 g it starves of oxygen without ventilation; at 0.16 g natural buoyancy induces ~6.8-7.5 cm/s (right at the minimum of the U-shaped LOI curve), so materials burn at lower O2 on the Moon (LOI ~13.7-14.5% O2) than on Earth (LOI ~16.5-18.0% O2)
Quantify the U-shaped Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) and flame spread rate under de Ris scaling at lunar gravity (0.16 g) versus 0 g and 1 g

sources.title: NASA Lunar 0.16g Partial Gravity (LUCI, FM2, ZGF, SEA 8.2 psia, HALO) — simulated values (team dataset)
NASA GRC / NTRS & PSI - Olson, Ferkul, T'ien & Liao Partial-Gravity Flammability · https://ntrs.nasa.gov / PSI SoFIE & BASS Partial-g Archive

modifications: Replace the terrestrial NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (1 g) certification with tests or correction factors at the minimum of the U-shaped LOI curve (equivalent flow of 6.5-8.0 cm/s for lunar 0.16 g)
Add the intrinsic buoyant velocity V_eff = sqrt(V_forced^2 + V_buoyant(g)^2) and de Ris scaling (V_f ~ (k*rho*c)^(-1) for thin solids) to the prediction engine

eva.name: Mars 0.38 g partial gravity: N2/Ar, MOXIE, ESD, fine water mist (team campaign)
eva.hardware: NASA GRC partial-gravity facilities / CO2-diluted burners (FLEX/ACME/SoFIE) / Mars ISRU architecture (MOXIE)
key_findings: At Martian gravity (0.38 g) the natural buoyant flow (~10.5 cm/s) falls exactly in the regime of maximum flame spread rate (the 10 cm/s HVAC risk peak); however, replacing part of the N2 with in-situ CO2 raises the LOI by +2.5% to +3.8% O2 thanks to its high molar heat capacity and radiative reabsorption in the 2.7 and 4.3 micron bands

Determine fire behavior at 0.38 g (where buoyant velocity matches the 10 cm/s peak spread rate) and quantify the effectiveness of CO2 extracted from the Martian atmosphere as a diluent and radiative suppressant
